text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: APAC1 ingress alert — surge in 502/504 + connection_resets reported across NLB -> Envoy mesh. Error rate 35% for last 5m, healthchecks failing in AZ-B targetgroup. Paging oncall.

alex-sre: I’m on it. seeing high envoy downstream errors `connection_reset` and a lot of 504s from ingress-controller upstreams. CPU ok, but socket waitqueue is growing. Dumping recent logs now.

alex-sre: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:15Z envoy upstream reset: ECONNRESET id=0x7f... route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T03:12:16Z healthcheck fail target=10.0.42.18:3080 status=unhealthy consecutive=6
```

mike-sre: I can see NLB targetgroup in AZ-B showing ~60% unhealthy, other AZs healthy. Some nodes reporting `ENETUNREACH` at kernel. Could be noisy NICs in AZ-B.

luis-net: AWS status? I'm checking AZ-B underlying host fleet. No public AWS event, but I see increased network errors from a subset of instances in eu/apac zone. Suggest reweight Route53 away from AZ-B to reduce blast radius.

priya-pm: CS flagged two enterprise customers in APAC seeing 50-70% API call errors. Need an impact list and ETA for mitigation.

tara-cs: Customer list attached (redacted): Acme Analytics, FinLend APAC org, several lower-tier tenants. We’re preparing a status update to send in ~10m.

alex-sre: Immediate plan: 1) scale ingress-controller replicas to absorb stuck connections and restart unhealthy pods 2) update envoy upstream timeout and enable circuit_breakers to fail fast for affected backends 3) shift DNS weight away from AZ-B (luis to confirm). Applying actions now.

alex-sre: scaling ingress:
```
kubectl -n ingress-system scale deploy/ingress-controller --replicas=8
kubectl rollout status deploy/ingress-controller -n ingress-system
```

opsbot: Deployment started: ingress-controller -> scale to 8 (started by alex-sre) :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout in progress, 2/8 ready.

mike-sre: Also bumping Envoy downstream keepalive to 90s and connection timeout to 20s to allow more graceful draining. Patching configmap.

mike-sre: envoy config patch:
```
clusters:
  - name: upstream-backend
    circuit_breakers:
      thresholds:
        - max_connections: 1200
          max_pending_requests: 500
          max_requests: 2000
```

luis-net: Started Route53 weight adjustment: AZ-B -> 10%, AZ-A -> 45%, AZ-C -> 45% (propagation expected ~30-60s). Monitoring DNS healthchecks now.

incident-bot: Route53 weights updated by luis-net. Healthcheck alarms suppressed during mitigation window.

alex-sre: After scaling + envoy patch + DNS shift error rate dropped from 35% -> 8% in 6m. Some residual 502s tied to specific host pairs. Still seeing connection resets from a group of instances in AZ-B.

mike-sre: Going to cordon and drain the suspect nodes in AZ-B and replace them. Taking one at a time to avoid capacity loss.

mike-sre: cordon/drain commands:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-42-18
kubectl drain ip-10-0-42-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

luis-net: Noted. Opening a ticket with our cloud provider to investigate NIC flapping on those hosts. Requesting replacement of 3 instances.

tara-cs: Drafted customer notice (short): "We're investigating reduced availability in APAC; mitigation underway. Some requests may see transient 5xx. We'll update in 15m." Approving to send.

priya-pm: Send it, tagging affected accounts. Also create a dashboard snapshot for postmortem.

alex-sre: Handing the incident to mike-sre for the next shift to finish host replacements and verify full recovery. I'll stay on-call for follow-ups. :handshake:

mike-sre: Taking over. Current status: errors ~3-8% across APAC, AZ-B residual resets but slowly declining as nodes are replaced. I'll coordinate with luis and ops. Filing incident ticket JIRA-INC-1021 for full RCA and timeline.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV-2. Pager suppressed for follow-on alerts until recovery.

luis-net: Confirmed cloud provider will reprovision instances; ETA 45m for replacement and network verification.

mike-sre: Next steps: complete host replacement in AZ-B, validate NLB health checks return to ~100%, revert Route53 weights when healthy, postmortem in #postmortems and JIRA-INC-1021. Assigning owners: mike-sre (mitigation), luis-net (network RCA), alex-sre (ingress tuning + follow-up), priya-pm (customer comms), tara-cs (customer notifications).

tara-cs: Sent customer note. :email: Will update when resolved.

alex-sre: Quick wins for the postmortem: add a runbook step to auto-redistribute DNS weights on sustained AZ targetgroup failures and a checklist for cordon/drain sequencing to avoid cascades.

mike-sre: Agreed. Also recommend adding NLB target-level connection metrics to our console and alert if connection_reset rate spikes >5% for 3m.

incident-bot: Thread marked resolved for active paging at 3165001820 by incident-bot. Follow-up remains in JIRA-INC-1021. :white_check_mark:"
